fields.description: Nothing on this page takes effect until a key is saved here. Two keys are used, for two different jobs: one is held by the server and never leaves it, the other is handed to the browser and must therefore be restricted.
fields.label: Google keys

fields.description: Used by the server alone. Addresses are looked up with it, and the small map pictures on task cards and pop-ups are fetched through it, so the key itself is never sent to a browser. While it is blank, addresses are not resolved and no map picture is drawn.
fields.label: Google Maps API Key (server)

fields.description: Used by the Near Me map alone. That map is drawn in the browser, so this key is sent to the browser and must be a separate key restricted to the site's own domains (HTTP referrer). While it is blank, Near Me reports that the map is not configured, and the doctor list still works.
fields.label: Google Maps Browser Key (Near Me)

fields.description: Required by the clustered pins on the Near Me map. A Map ID is created in Google Cloud Console under Maps > Map IDs, as the JavaScript type. While it is blank, Google's DEMO_MAP_ID is used, which draws a working but unstyled map and is not intended for production.
fields.label: Google Maps Map ID (Near Me)

fields.description: An address is looked up with the saved server key and the result is shown here, which proves that the key, the billing account and the Geocoding API are all live. The page must be saved first.
fields.label: Check Connection

fields.description: Where a doctor's clinic is searched for: the Desk 'Set Clinic Location' picker, and the search box on Near Me.
fields.label: Address search

fields.description: Addresses are always resolved by Google, whichever provider draws the maps below. Shown for information; it cannot be changed.
fields.label: Geocoding Provider

fields.description: The two-letter country the address search is confined to, such as IN for India or AE for the United Arab Emirates. An address outside that country is not offered as a result, so this must name the country the doctors are actually in. While it is blank, the whole world is searched.
fields.label: Address Search Country

fields.description: Who draws each map. Only the small, still map pictures have a choice: Near Me is always a Google map, because it is interactive. OpenStreetMap costs nothing and needs no key; Google is charged per view and needs the server key above.
fields.label: Map display

fields.description: Draws the small map on a task card, inside the task pop-up, and in the Desk activity list. While it is blank, OpenStreetMap is used.
fields.label: Thumbnail Map Provider

fields.description: Draws the larger map inside the visit pop-ups, where a capture is confirmed or an out-of-range visit is refused. While it is blank, Google is used.
fields.label: Dialog Map Provider

fields.description: How closely the small map pictures are zoomed onto their pin. A higher number is closer. While it is blank, 16 is used.
fields.label: Map Thumbnail Zoom

fields.description: Advanced. Where the OpenStreetMap maps above fetch their tiles, given as a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template. While it is blank, the free public tiles are used, which are rate-limited; under heavy traffic this should point at an owned or paid tile server.
fields.label: OpenStreetMap Tile URL

fields.description: Which leads a visit is checked against, and who may correct a clinic's pin. This is what the location capture on an in-person activity is measured with.
fields.label: Visit location tracking

fields.description: The lead groups whose in-person visits must be logged at the doctor's clinic, each with the distance allowed from it. A lead outside every group listed here is never asked for a location. While the table is empty, no visit is checked.
fields.label: Location-Tracked Grains

fields.description: The role allowed to move a clinic's pin once it has been set, which is how a wrong or outdated location is corrected. While it is blank, only System Manager may move a pin.
fields.label: Manager Override Role
